Files and search

read_file, list_dir, grep, and glob inspect the workspace. write_file creates or replaces a file; edit_file makes an exact replacement. File writes to the same path serialize; unrelated files can proceed concurrently.

READ BEFORE WRITE

Existing files normally must be read before write_file will replace them. This guard prevents blind overwrites. edit_file instead fails if its exact old text does not match.

Commands and persistent compute

ToolWhat it does
shellRuns a command and captures stdout, stderr, and exit status.
processStarts and controls long-lived background or interactive processes.
pykernelRuns persistent Python; values and imports survive calls.
bun_replRuns persistent JavaScript or TypeScript with top-level await.

Use the persistent tools when a task benefits from retained state. bun_repl uses the Bun executable already on PATH; it does not install packages.

Large output

Tool output is capped to protect the context window. When a result is truncated, use read_tool_result with its call ID and offset to retrieve the original output in pages. In the terminal UI, /expand <n> shows the full output of a recent tool call.
